memory_update.text: COHR and LITE are the primary reference leaders for direct InP/laser/optical-component exposure in AI datacenter photonics.

AXTI should be tracked as an underfollowed substrate-layer candidate for InP wafer exposure, but survival to later layers depends on verifying AI datacenter customer linkage, backlog quality, and capacity expansion economics.
ALMU belongs only in the speculative shadow lane until commercial qualification, material AI-photonics revenue, and customer evidence are confirmed; financing and dilution risk must be checked.
The node appears to split into three public-market sublayers: established InP/device leaders, substrate/wafer suppliers, and emerging alternative compound-semiconductor integration platforms.
Need a separate pass for equipment and test/measurement enablers around MOCVD, wafer inspection, photonic test, burn-in, and optical transceiver manufacturing services.

node: Photonic components: InP lasers, photodetectors, precision substrates, and compound-semiconductor platforms
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the AI photonics component node. The clearest reference leaders are Coherent and Lumentum because both sit directly in InP, lasers, optical engines, transceivers, and AI data-center optical interconnects. The underfollowed lane adds AXT as a substrate-level candidate tied to InP wafer supply. Aeluma is included only as a speculative shadow candidate because it targets scalable III-V-on-silicon / compound-semiconductor platforms for AI photonics but still requires commercial qualification, revenue scale, customer evidence, and financing-risk verification.
